10.text: Ainu do not drive reindeer either with snowshoes or in any

11.text: other way. My own experience and the opinion of the natives

12.text: both contradict Nordenskiöld when he speaks of the clumsiness

13.text: of these snowshoes. The Lamut, who are the best snowshoe-

14.text: runners in northeastern Asia, achieve wonders with this partic-

15.text: ular kind of shoe. Several times I had Lamut runners wearing

16.text: such snowshoes who accompanied my dog-team for miles and

17.text: miles without any visible strain. The dogs ran in the deep,

18.text: hard-beaten track. The Lamut runners glided by their side

19.text: over the surface of the snow. Races on such snowshoes are

20.text: also run among the Lamut runners, in which they attain a

21.text: speed equal to that of the fastest race-reindeer.

22.text: The other variety of snowshoe, and the one typical of

23.text: the Chukchee (Fig. 193, b), is the so-called “raven feet”

24.text: (veˊlvɪ-yeˊhɪt; in local Russian, лапки, “paws,” which is evidently

25.text: a translation of the same term). They are made with a wooden

26.text: frame, rather small in size (60-70 cm. by 16-20 cm.), and inter-

27.text: laced with thongs. The frame is rounded between the two

31.text: Netted snowshoes are used by natives when walking on

32.text: uneven ground, where the other kind of shoe would be quite

33.text: useless. Herdsmen, for example, wear them when tending the

34.text: reindeer in the pastures, where the snow is scraped and ploughed

35.text: up by the feet of the animals. Seal-hunters also wear them

36.text: in walking on the outskirts of the rugged ice.

37.text: Snowshoes having a similar name are in use also among

38.text: the Koryak. Their construction is essentially the same, only

39.text: the frame is more elongated. Snowshoes of this kind are

40.text: also well known in America among the Eskimo and the

41.text: northern Indians from the Pacific to the Atlantic Ocean.
